I can’t produce a bitmap image here because no image-generation tool is available. I won’t pretend one was created. Instead, below are two useful alternatives you can use immediately:

1) A ready-to-paste image-generation prompt (for Stable Diffusion / Midjourney / DALL·E etc.)
Copy and paste this into your image tool and set aspect ratio to 1:1 (square). Adjust model-specific parameters as needed.

Prompt:
"Square watercolor illustration of a solitary lighthouse in dense fog. Soft, wet-on-wet watercolor style on textured cold-press paper; delicate granulation and soft bloom edges. Composition: lighthouse slightly off-center, mid-ground on rocky outcrop, low horizon, misty sea fading into fog. Color palette: muted desaturated blues, soft cool grays, pale warm cream for lighthouse, a faint warm amber glow from the beacon. Lighting: diffused, atmospheric, low contrast, subtle backlight through fog. Brushwork: loose washes for sky and fog, layered glazing for lighthouse form, minimal sharp detail—only a few crisp highlights on beacon and rock edges. Mood: quiet, contemplative, ethereal. High watercolor authenticity: visible paper texture, pigment granulation, gentle bleeds, subtle brushstrokes. Square composition, 1:1."

Negative prompt / instructions to avoid:
"no photorealism, no high-detail digital rendering, avoid harsh outlines, no people, no modern buildings, no text or logos."

2) Step-by-step watercolor painting instructions to make it by hand
Materials:
- Cold-press watercolor paper (300gsm), square sheet
- Winsor & Newton or similar watercolors, brushes: large flat or mop brush for washes, round size 6–10 for mid details, small round or rigger for beacon highlight
- Masking fluid (optional), tissue, spray bottle, palette, clean water

Steps:
1. Light pencil sketch: mark horizon low, position lighthouse slightly off-center, indicate rocky base and a faint sea line.
2. Wet the sky area with clean water (wet-on-wet). Drop in diluted ultramarine + cerulean blue and a touch of neutral gray. Tilt the paper slightly so pigments flow; leave central area paler for fog.
3. While still damp, use a clean damp brush or spray bottle to lift some pigment to create soft foggy gaps. Let dry slightly.
4. Block in sea with horizontal washes of desaturated blue-gray, keeping edges soft where sea meets fog. Use a tissue to soften any hard lines.
5. Paint the rocky outcrop with an underwash of warm gray (mix of burnt umber + ultramarine), letting pigment granulate. Add a second, darker layer for shadows after first dries.
6. Mask the lighthouse base (masking fluid) if you want to keep it very clean. Otherwise, paint it with a light warm-cream wash (very diluted yellow ochre + titanium white if using gouache for highlights). Keep edges slightly softened where fog touches it.
7. Build subtle form with two or three glazing layers—cooler shadow mixes on shaded side (ultramarine + burnt sienna), warmer touches where the fog thins.
8. Beacon glow: while lighthouse area is dry, glaze a small soft halo with a diluted warm amber (cadmium yellow + a touch of alizarin crimson). Use a tiny brush to place a brighter dot for the light; soften edges with a damp brush.
9. Add minimal crisp details last (railings, a ladder line) sparingly—leave most edges soft. Use a drybrush or small stroke to suggest rock texture.
10. Final touches: lift tiny highlights with a damp brush or add a touch of opaque white gouache to the beacon and a few sea highlights. Remove masking fluid and add any necessary softening.
11. Let dry completely; scan or photograph at high resolution if you want a digital copy.

If you’d like, I can:
- Tailor the generation prompt for a specific tool (Midjourney, Stable Diffusion, etc.)
- Provide a printable tracing layout as line instructions (text only) you can trace manually
Tell me which option you prefer.
